items.title: Ernest Poree Interview, 1975-10-16
items.q: Who told you that? Mr. Lazarus.

ctx.x: He used to tell me about all the different places he'd be at home. You know, I mean, just for kicks, he'd be going around all these places. That's right. And yet I knew he'd be working three jobs. I couldn't see how he could work in the paddock, and clean up the theaters, and clean up the wax museum, and still have time for all that fun.

That's right. He sure did. He sure did. When did he sleep? Sure again, the- He got about an hour or so sleep with him. That's what his boss told me. I played for them at Prince Coni. I went out and he said, he used to tell George all the time, he's doing too much work. He said, George, your in-laws, haunt. Who told you that? Mr. Lazarus. Oh, yeah. And he said that he told George to quit doing all that work. If he needed that money, call him to him. He would help his mom, he said, doing all that work. Say, all…
He'd have his little grandson, a great-grandson or something. Yeah, little grandson, yeah. His grandson, I remember that.
